low.title: Restart reconciliation of an interrupted promotion records no unreviewed remote change when the destination no longer matches, although the rename may already have happened
low.boundary: D2 contract: a promotion that fails after its rename records an unreviewed remote change. In-process failure does this (promotionFailed). Restart reconciliation does not.
low.reproduction: Stage and promote a change; the process dies after writePromoted's rename but before the PROMOTING->PROMOTED transition. Between the crash and the restart, the destination is edited, so its sha256 no longer equals contentHash. Restart reconciliation sets the record FAILED ('the promotion did not complete') and calls no recordRemoteChange, so the project changed by the rename is not listed for review, even though promotionStarted=true already counts it in mutationSequence.
low.evidence: manager.server.ts ~4556-4564: for PROMOTING records, landed = destinationState(...).sha256 === contentHash; the else branch only calls staging.transition(...FAILED). Compare manager.server.ts promotionFailed ~2675-2679, which calls store.recordRemoteChange.
low.repair: In the not-landed branch, record an unreviewed remote change for record.destination (as promotionFailed does) whenever record.promotionStarted is true, or whenever the destination differs from destinationBefore. Add a regression that simulates the crash-after-rename-then-edit case.

votes.reasoning:
Not refuted. The finding reproduces on the current working tree.

Probe: `node --experimental-strip-types scratchpad/review-probes/r2/probe1.mts` (base = review-probes/r2/proj, content "hello", operation write) prints:
- `.augment/rules.md` -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT (plain document)
- `AUGMEN~1/rules.md` -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT
- `.qwen/commands/c.md` -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT
- `QWEN~1/commands/c.md` -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT
- `.warp/w.md` -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT
- `WARP~1/w.md` -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT

Controls that do classify correctly, so the gap is specific to these directories: `.claude/rules.md`, `.github/instructions/a.md`, `.trae/rules/r.md` and `.cursor/rules/r.md` return AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.

Root cause: src/lib/bunny-missions/authorization.server.ts:525 (AGENT_INSTRUCTION_DIR) lists .claude, .cursor, .codex, .gemini, .continue, .clinerules, .windsurf, .roo, .kiro, .aider, .grok, .agents, .amazonq, .junie, .opencode, .cline and generic rules/skills/prompts/instructions names, but not .augment, .qwen or .warp. The file-name regex at :524 covers only root-level names such as qwen.md and warp.md, so the directories fall through. Line :602-603 then passes, and the leaf/dir checks at :604-631 reach PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT at :631 for any .md/.txt file. Because :631 is the only gate, deviceWriteClassRefusal (:636-638) returns null, and remoteExecutionRefusal (authorization.server.ts:244-254) lets the write through to staging.

Impact in the current tree: manager.server.ts:2506 stages the write with classification PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT, and it is not promoted without Windows Host review (manager.server.ts:2224 and :2297 attach DEVICE_REVIEW_REASON). So the device cannot land the file without the desktop approving it, which is why this is MEDIUM rather than HIGH. The defect is that the reviewer and the audit trail are told the file is a plain document when it is an agent instruction file that agents (Augment, Qwen, Warp) load as standing instructions. The contract says agent instruction locations are never PHONE_SAFE, and this violates it. Existing tests (f02-staging.test.ts:635-638 and :662-666) do not cover these three directories, which explains why they were missed.

Not intended behavior: the directory list is explicit and the other agent tools are listed, so the omission is a gap rather than a documented exception. Remaining scope to note: any non-rules file such as `.augment/guidelines.md` or `.warp/notes.md` takes the same path.

Suggested fix: add `\.augment|\.qwen|\.warp` (and any other agent-tool dot folders) to AGENT_INSTRUCTION_DIR, plus regression cases in f02-staging.test.ts for `.augment/`, `.qwen/`, `.warp/` and their 8.3 forms.

Confirmed against the working tree. Probe at scratchpad/review-probes/r2/skeptic-repairs-1/cls.mts imports classifyDeviceWrite from the repo. Results: .augment/rules.md, .qwen/commands/c.md, .warp/w.md, AUGMEN~1/rules.md and QWEN~1/commands/c.md all classify PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT ("plain document"). Control cases are correctly AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS: .claude/rules.md, .augment/rules/x.mdc, .qwen/QWEN.md, WARP.md, .roo/rules.md. Cause: authorization.server.ts:525 AGENT_INSTRUCTION_DIR has no .augment, .qwen or .warp entry, and the AGENT_INSTRUCTION_FILE leaf regex (line 524) does not match rules.md, commands/*.md or w.md. The classifier therefore falls through to the document branch. Remote path: remoteExecutionRefusal (authorization.server.ts ~244-254) calls deviceWriteClassRefusal (line 636-638), which returns null for PHONE_SAFE classes, so a phone write is admitted and staged. Mitigations that limit severity: the write is staged inertly, and promotion needs the Host-side review, so no direct code execution or unreviewed mutation was shown. Realistic gap is .augment/commands/*.md and .qwen/commands/*.md, which are real agent-command locations; .augment/rules/*.md is covered by the rules dir entry. Round-1 claim that .augment/ is AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS is not true in this tree. Severity MEDIUM stands (contract violation with a plausible persistence path into agent tooling, gated by desktop promotion review).

votes.reasoning: Not refuted. Probe review-probes/r2/skeptic-repairs-0/probe-esc.mts imports the live staging.server.ts escapedText and feeds it U+200F, U+200E, U+061C, U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF and U+2060. All eight come back RAW in the output; only U+202E and U+2066 are escaped. This matches the regex at staging.server.ts:181, which covers only •,  ,  , ‪-‮ and ⁦-⁩. JSON.stringify (staging.server.ts:181) does not escape any of the flagged code points. promotionReason (manager.server.ts:2536-2537) embeds that output unchanged into the approval reason. The finding's repro is accurate. Caveats: (1) F02_CONTRACT.md line 38 only says "full JSON-escaped content"; it does not explicitly require bidi escaping. The stronger requirement is the intent stated in the escapedText code comment. (2) The probe shows the bytes are present in the string. It does not render the Windows Host UI, so the visual reordering or hiding is inferred, not observed. Impact is limited: the approval is bound to contentHash and destination, so no authority is gained. The gap is in review integrity for the human gate, which fits MEDIUM. Related note: the same gap also exists for destination (manager.server.ts:2539 uses JSON.stringify(record.destination) without escaping). The round-1 repair therefore looks incomplete, and this is a valid re-report.

Partly real, overstated in severity and mechanism.

Real part (probe: scratchpad/review-probes/r2/skeptic-repairs-1/esc-check.mts, run with node --experimental-strip-types): staging.server.ts:181 escapedText() escapes only U+2022, U+2028-2029, U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069 after JSON.stringify. Output for "ok ‏‎؜ end" still contains raw 200f, 200e and 061c. Those three are Bidi_Control characters (Unicode PropList), so the comment "bidi controls are escaped" and the contract's bidi-escaping requirement are not met for them. Zero-width U+200B-200D, U+FEFF and U+2060 are also left raw. The round-1 repair is incomplete for content: the destination is now covered by the Cf/Cc refusal at authorization.server.ts:577, but the content in manager.server.ts:2536-2537 is not.

Why not MEDIUM: the approval is bound to structured fields (contentHash, contentSize, destination) that the Host checks, so the approver cannot be made to approve different bytes. JSON quoting does escape quote and backslash (probe: quote-injection input yields \" escapes), so the claimed "imitate prompt structure" path does not work; RLM/LRM/ALM can only shift the visual order of neutral punctuation, and only if the Host UI renders bidi. Zero-width characters hide nothing visible here, they only make the glyphs shown differ from the bytes. That is a review-integrity and defense-in-depth gap with no authority change, so LOW fits. The probe cannot demonstrate the on-screen reordering because no bidi renderer runs in this sandbox, so the reorder effect is unverified.

Suggested fix: extend the regex to /[\p{Cf}\p{Cc}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}]/gu (escape to \uXXXX) in escapedText and apply the same to the destination, source and reasons text in promotionReason. Add a test with U+200F in content.

Refuted as a MEDIUM audit-integrity finding. Code reading only (no probe run, no npm test, no repo edits).

1. The premise "an admission uses the answer" is not how the implementation models it. Under the implemented model the answer is still live while the step is running, so revoking it mid-run removes remaining authority.

2. Revocation during the running window therefore ends live authority, which is the intended behavior. endDeviceAnswers (manager.server.ts:2427-2441) correctly clears approvedOnce and stamps INVALIDATED_BY_DEVICE_REVOCATION / INVALIDATED_BY_SIGNOUT. The stamp matches what happened: the answer stopped authorizing and was not carried to completion. No authority is gained or retained. The reproduction's step 4 (completion without CONSUMED) is real only in the narrow sense that the step completes after the answer was cleared. That is an audit-label question, not a security one.

3. Documented contract: F02_CONTRACT.md describes an answer that is "unused" when ended by revocation or sign-out, and CONSUMED on promotion success. Neither line defines "used" as admission. The finding's standard ("already authorized an admission must read as used") is not in the contract.

Residual, if one wanted to keep it open: a step that keeps running after revocation and then completes is recorded with INVALIDATED_* rather than CONSUMED, and the record does not say the answer partially authorized work before it ended. That is at most a LOW labeling/clarity item. It has no authority impact, so it does not meet the MEDIUM bar.

Evidence checked: manager.server.ts:1550-1564, 1636-1642, 2427-2441, 2456-2482, 3568, http.server.ts:842, F02_CONTRACT.md lines 52, 70, 79, 86-92, and remote-authority.test.ts:1457-1460 (asserts approvedOnce cleared on revocation, not a stamp label).

(2) endDeviceAnswers (manager.server.ts:2427-2441) skips only completed/skipped/failed/stopped, so a running step with approvedOnce is processed. A later allow_once hits the guard at 2611 and throws an explicit CommandRefusedError before any write, so there is no mutation and no authority gap. A deny path exists: respond at 4002-4004 calls staging.transition, which returns null for a FAILED record without throwing, and then saveRequest resolves the request, so the workstation can still close it. The restart reconciliation at 4556-4563 also marks FAILED without closing the request. The finding's "silently refused forever" wording is inaccurate because each retry gets an explicit refusal and deny always resolves. Stop/revocation close the request only through endStaged (2559-2590), which promotionFailed does not call. The real defect is a state-machine liveness gap: a post-write failure leaves a waiting step with pendingRequestId set until the workstation denies or stops the Mission.
